kids: 🎨 Choose your own theme: Football (any team), Space, Animals or Music & art — even the questions change!
items: 🖥️ Wide screens use the space: Today shows the next best thing beside today’s plan; Practise and Mock exam have missions on the left, the question in the middle and the coach and game modes on the right; Rewards puts your player beside medals and the leaderboard. Phones still stack.
⚙️ The menu now drops down under its button instead of hiding behind the header.

🎨 Themes (⚙️ Menu → 🎨 Theme), chosen per child: ⚽ Anfield (the original), ⚽ Football — my team (any club name and team colour), 🚀 Space, 🐾 Animals & nature and 🎵 Music & art. Each changes the colours, background, header and sticker, and the stories in the questions — in practice and in Starlane — while the maths stays the same.

kids: 🧭 A tidier app: Today, Practise, Mock exam, Learn and Rewards along the top (or the bottom on a phone)
items: 🧭 New layout: the home page is organised into five areas — 🎯 Today (with one big “next best thing” button), ✏️ Practise, 🏆 Mock exam, 📚 Learn and 🎁 Rewards — shown one at a time, with the bar at the bottom on phones. Starting practice from anywhere jumps to Practise; “⛶ Focus on the question” hides everything else. The header buttons (switch player, help, sound, voices, install) are in ⚙️ Menu, and the save banner shrinks to a chip once progress is saved.

👪 Parent dashboard regrouped: Overview (summary cards), 📋 Plan (exam plan and key dates), 📈 Progress (readiness, focus areas, topics, question types, mocks, learning), ⏱️ Time & activity, 🎮 Games & rewards (Starlane, shop) and ⚙️ Settings & data — plus a “find anything” box.
📱 Fixed: on narrow phones the save banner no longer makes the page scroll sideways.

kids: ⬆️ Questions now get harder as you get them right — just like the real ISEB test
items: ⬆️ Difficulty levels for every exam: each question type is rated easy, medium or hard, and the numbers lean smaller at Warm-up and bigger at Stretch. Match-day practice and mocks are now adaptive — three right first time in a row steps up a level, two misses steps down — like the real adaptive ISEB Pre-Test. Warm-up and Boss stay as fixed levels. Starlane follows the child’s level too.

✏️ Twelve new stretch question types within the Year 5 curriculum for Tiffin, the 11+ grammars and the ISEB Pre-Test: square and cube numbers, primes, factors, L-shaped areas and perimeters, chained percentages, fractions of a remainder, Roman numerals, “who am I?” number clues, negative temperatures, overnight timetables and decimal calculations.
🧹 Questions that came out too easy by accident (equal ratio parts such as 5:5, fractions like 4/4, × 1 or + 0) are thrown away and made again.
⏱ Quick-fire exams show a pace guide (about a minute a question) and the current level on the question screen.

kids: 🎯 The top of the app now shows which school and test you are training for, with a countdown
items: 🎯 Exam plan: each child has a plan of tests (test, school, date, result). The app trains for the next upcoming one, and moves on when a test has passed. The header shows it — “Training for: Eton College — ISEB Common Pre-Test · 30 November 2026 · 17 days to go” — with a countdown sticker in the last 60 days. Tapping it opens the plan (grown-ups only).

📈 Readiness for the chosen exam, topic by topic (including maths answered in Starlane), with a printable report; 📅 key dates for the plan’s exams from the official timelines (Tiffin, ISEB, Eton, Common Entrance).
🏆 Mocks follow the exam: question count, timing and multiple choice where the real test uses it.
➕ Adding a player now asks what they are preparing for (or “not sure yet”) and their school.

✏️ New original questions for 13+ Common Entrance / scholarship (algebra, probability, polygons, circles, prisms, reverse percentages, the nth term, indices, compound interest) and quick-fire questions for Tiffin Stage 1, 11+ grammar and the ISEB Pre-Test. Each is only used for those exams, in practice and in Starlane.

🚀 Starlane maths in the parent overview: each maths question answered in Starlane is recorded with where it came from (the child’s exam and topic, or Starlane’s own space questions) and whether it was right, with a weekly summary and the recent questions.

🔍 “Check Starlane questions” on the parent overview opens Starlane in the background and asks it for 10 questions through the same connection the game uses — showing each question’s source and a ✅ if they match the chosen exam. No playing needed.

📚 Exam sources updated after the exam-watch agent’s first run: Tiffin’s illustrative maths questions, its admissions FAQs and Tiffin Girls’ Year 7 page; GL Assessment’s free familiarisation materials (new address); ISEB’s Pre-Test page for families and the 13+ Common Entrance timetable. Eton’s site blocks automated checks, so the agent now lists it to check by hand.

kids: 🎓 Practice now follows the exam you are preparing for
items: 🎓 Exam profiles: Tiffin Stage 1, Tiffin Stage 2, 11+ grammar (multiple choice), ISEB Common Pre-Test (Eton, Harrow and others) and 13+ Common Entrance / scholarship. Each child picks one in the parent overview (“🎓 Exam & sources”); mixed and focus practice weight topics to match it. Existing children are recognised from their exam name — Apollo stays on Tiffin Stage 2.

📚 Sources: each exam lists the official pages our original questions are modelled on (Tiffin’s illustrative questions and admissions policy, ISEB, Eton and Harrow admissions and scholarship pages), with the date they were last checked.
🚀 Starlane’s maths questions now follow the child’s exam, whether played from the Starlane site or the built-in copy.

🤖 Exam-watch agent (tools/exam-watch): a scheduled GitHub Action that checks the official pages and admissions news, drafts and double-checks new original questions, and opens a pull request with a report for review.

kids: 🚀 Starlane now opens from its own website inside ApolloMaths — same game, same saved commander
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader now runs from its own site (stuartokin.github.io/Starlane) when opened from the arcade: one shared copy of the game. ApolloMaths passes the child’s name, level and question bank, keeps the saved commander in the child’s progress, runs the grown-up check for test mode, and records the score when the player leaves. Arcade play time still counts. If the Starlane site cannot be reached, a message offers to try again or play the built-in copy, which stays as a fallback.

🚀 Starlane Trader: the game file now has a question socket (window.StarlaneQuestions) so the standalone Starlane site and ApolloMaths can supply its maths questions; the game files are identical in both repos. No change in play.

kids: 🎬 Trailer polish: a longer opening star and end card
items: 🎬 Starlane Trader trailer: the opening star (2.8 s, swelling slowly) and the end card (5.5 s) last longer for anticipation, and the small yellow outside-camera aiming square no longer appears in videos.
